title: Define dynamic surface rhythm and anchor contrast for tokens, spacing, and elevation
creator: Maya Fernández
description: Problem: Several components (tables, charts, buttons) exhibit visual instability when content density or zoom changes. Current token set has edge cases: inconsistent overlay contrast, conflicting radius scales, and non-linear elevation steps that produce perceived jumping. Goal: produce a small, opinionated token update that introduces a dynamic surface rhythm (density-aware spacing/radius scales), an anchor-driven color contrast system for interactive surfaces, and a simplified elevation hierarchy with perceptually uniform steps. Deliverables: token proposal JSON, migration guide for components, Figma token file, and a short rollout plan for staged release (dev flag, canary components, and a migration checklist). Links: Figma exploration: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/dynamic-surface-rhythm, PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Dynamic+Surface+Rhythm, design tokens draft: https://drive.google.com/file/d/EXAMPLE, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/284
comments: 2025-07-11 — Kickoff with PM and Frontend: scoped to token changes only; avoid renaming existing tokens to minimize surface churn.

2025-07-18 — Figma MVP uploaded; two alternatives for radius scaling: 'linear-radius' (px-based) and 'proportional-radius' (percentage of control height). Team lean: proportional better for responsive controls, but requires small CSS helper layer.

2025-07-22 — Accessibility review (Aisha Patel): requested contrast checks for interactive anchors and hover elevations at 2x and 4x density. Action: include example states in the token spec and run automated color contrast tests.

2025-07-29 — Engineering review (Martin O'Leary): Kernel concern flagged for chart shadows — recommends limiting elevation token palette for canvas-painted shadows to z0,z2,z4 to reduce repaint cost. Added as constraint in design doc.

2025-08-01 — Prototype PR created: demo page shows table rows at 3 densities and button radius scaling. Early feedback: small icon buttons look cramped with proportional-radius; proposed small-size token adjustment for icon-only controls.

2025-08-04 — Decision log: adopt 'dynamic-surface' token group that exposes density variants (default, compact, dense) and an 'anchor-contrast' family for primary/secondary/neutral interactive surfaces. Elevation reduced to perceptually-even stops: z0,z1,z2,z3,z5. Next: author migration guide and schedule rollout to canary components (buttons, table rows, chart cards).
